The masculine singular 'he' here is the unmarked (zero-suffix) form — there is no separate person ending; the final -a is the inherent stem vowel of the base pattern, not a person or tense suffix.

9.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
9.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

10.meaning: 'He turned (His attention) to', 'He settled upon', or 'He became evenly established' — a verb of rising to / directing oneself toward something and setting it in balanced order; depending on context it can mean to mount, to settle over, or to become level and complete.
10.grammar: Past tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'). It is a form X verb (the istaf'ala pattern, marked by the sīn-tā' prefix placed before the root, often adding a reflexive or 'seeking/becoming' sense). The final long -ā is how the past-tense 'he' ending appears on verbs whose last root letter is a weak vowel; the initial i- is a helping vowel needed to begin the word.

11.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
11.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).

7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

8.meaning: The night — the period of darkness from sunset to dawn.
8.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' merges with the word's initial 'l', said al-layl). A noun for night-time. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… OF the night').

9.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
9.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

10.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
10.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

11.meaning: "Of what is within / the contents of" — literally 'with that which possesses', an idiom for the innermost contents or true nature of something. The feminine word dhāt means 'possessor of' and so 'that which holds/contains'.
11.grammar: The feminine noun 'dhāt' ('possessor/owner of') governed by the preposition 'bi-', hence the genitive -i ending used after prepositions. 'Dhāt' is grammatically a construct word: it expects a following noun, giving the sense 'that which holds/contains …'.
11.root: — (function word built on the idea of 'possessor of')

12.meaning: "The breasts / chests" — the chests of human beings, commonly used as the seat of the heart, feelings, intentions, and innermost thoughts.
12.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the chests'). The -i ending is the genitive case, typically linking it to a preceding word ('… OF …') or following a preposition. 'Ṣudūr' is the plural of 'ṣadr' (chest/breast).
12.root: ص-د-ر (ṣ-d-r) — chest, breast, the foremost part

1.meaning: 'Believe!' — a command to a group: have faith, trust, and affirm. Built on the verb meaning to attain security and to believe, it calls people to embrace faith.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb on the causative (Form IV) pattern, from the verb meaning 'to believe / to have faith'. The -ū ending directs the command to a second-person masculine plural audience, 'you all — believe!'.

2.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
2.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
2.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

3.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and His Messenger' — referring to one who is sent, an envoy or apostle bearing a message, joined by 'and' and possessed by 'His.'
3.grammar: 'Messenger' joined by wa- ('and') and followed by the possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, here because the word is linked in possession ('Messenger OF Him'); the pronoun takes the -hi form (with i-vowel) when it follows an i-sound.
3.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching; a message or one who is sent

4.meaning: A command meaning 'and spend, give out, expend (you, plural).' Form IV (anfaqa) of the root, denoting the disbursing of wealth or resources — spending in a cause or on others.
4.grammar: An imperative (command) to a plural 'you,' joined by wa- ('and'). The -ū ending directs the order to a masculine plural group ('all of you, spend…').

5.meaning: From what / from that which — a fusion of the preposition 'from' with the relative 'what/which', introducing the thing or situation being referred to.
5.grammar: A merger of 'min' ('from') and 'mā' ('what/that which'); the 'n' of 'min' assimilates into the 'm' of 'mā', doubling it. The combination means 'from what ...' and typically introduces a following clause describing the thing referred to. Being particles, neither part takes a case ending.

6.meaning: He made you, He appointed/rendered you (plural) — to bring into a state or set in a role. The verb can mean 'to make/create' or 'to designate as', with the attached object 'you (all)'.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he …'); the bare stem with the open ending marks completed action. The attached -kum is the second-person masculine plural object pronoun 'you all'. So: 'He made/appointed you (all)'.

8.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
8.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

9.meaning: 'So those who / then they who' — a connective 'so/then' joined to a relative pronoun meaning 'those who' (a masculine plural group identified by what follows).
9.grammar: A connective fa- ('so/then') on a relative pronoun. 'Alladhīna means 'those who / the ones who' and introduces a description; it refers to a masculine plural group and its form does not change for case.

10.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
10.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

11.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
11.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
11.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

12.meaning: And they spent or laid out — to disburse wealth, expending it (especially in giving and charitable outlay).
12.grammar: A past-tense verb (form IV) prefixed with 'wa' (and). The suffix '-ū' is the subject ending for a third-person masculine plural — 'they (did it)' — marking a completed action carried out by a group.

13.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
13.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

14.meaning: Means 'a reward, a wage, a recompense'. The word denotes the due return for work or deeds — payment earned, compensation, or a reward.
14.grammar: A noun in the nominative, indefinite ('a reward'). The -un ending (a doubled-vowel tanwīn) marks both indefiniteness ('a/some') and the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or for a thing being asserted to exist ('there is a reward').

15.meaning: Great, big, grave, weighty — large in size, importance, or seriousness.
15.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern conveying an intense, established quality ('great'). The final -un (nominative with nunation) marks it as indefinite and as a predicate or describing word ('is great'), not an object.

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
2.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

3.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

4.meaning: you believe / you have faith — to trust and affirm with conviction, especially faith in Allah and what He has revealed. The verb denotes ongoing, present believing.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb of Form IV (āmana), which makes the act of believing/granting security. The tu- prefix marks a 'you' subject, and the ending -ūna marks masculine plural and the indicative mood (a plain, ongoing statement: 'you all believe'). The -na would drop if a governing particle put it in another mood. The hamzah at the start of the stem belongs to the root.

5.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
5.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
5.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

7.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he calls / summons / invites you (plural)' — to call out to someone, beckoning or summoning them.
7.grammar: An imperfect (present/ongoing) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The ya- prefix marks 'he'; the verb ends in the weak long vowel -ū of its root. The attached -kum is the direct object 'you all'.
7.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invite, supplicate

9.meaning: 'By/in your Lord' — combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the noun 'Lord' (the Master, Sustainer, and Nurturer who owns, provides for, and brings to maturity) with the pronoun 'your (plural)'.
9.grammar: A preposition attached to a noun carrying a possessive pronoun. The preposition bi- ('with/by/in') puts the noun into the genitive case, reflected in the -i vowel of rabbi. The suffix -kum means 'your' addressing a plural group.
9.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord, master, to nurture and sustain

10.meaning: 'And indeed / while already' — the word 'wa' ('and, while') joined to 'qad', a particle that, before a past-tense verb, stresses that the action has certainly and already happened.
10.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and', or circumstantial 'while') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' emphasizes completion and certainty ('has indeed already…'); with a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes' or 'may'.

11.meaning: He took, he seized — a past-tense verb meaning to take hold of, receive, or take up. With certain objects (like a covenant or pledge) it carries the sense of formally taking or binding. The subject is 'he'.
11.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The bare stem with the final -a marks a completed action by a 'he' (third-person masculine singular) subject — 'he took'.

12.meaning: "Your covenant / solemn pledge" — a firm, binding agreement or pledge solemnly entered into; bound to a 'your' (plural).
12.grammar: A masculine singular noun with the attached possessive pronoun 'kum' ('your', plural). The -a before the pronoun is the accusative case ending, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).
12.root: و-ث-ق (w-th-q) — to be firm / bind / make a trustworthy pact

13.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
13.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

14.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
14.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
14.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

15.meaning: 'Believers / faithful ones' — the plural of muʾmin, one who has faith and trust in Allah and grants assent to the truth.

parts.en: believers (form IV participle, oblique masculine sound plural)

15.grammar: An active participle ('one who believes') from the form IV pattern, here a masculine sound plural. The single suffix -īna is the oblique (accusative/genitive) form of the masculine plural — used for a direct object or after a preposition — as opposed to the -ūna form used for the subject. Its nūn is part of the one ending and is not a separable morpheme.
15.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust; hence faith and belief

1.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
1.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'he sends down' or 'he causes to descend' — to bring something down from a higher place, often used of Allah sending down revelation, rain, or blessings. The doubled middle root letter conveys sending down gradually, repeatedly, or in stages.
3.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular: 'he' does the action. The yu- prefix is simply the 3rd-person masculine imperfect marker. What makes this Form II is the doubled middle root letter (the shaddah on the z: nazzil), a pattern that adds intensity or a gradual, repeated sense ('to send down in stages'). The final -u is the indicative ending, marking an ordinary statement of ongoing or habitual action.

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

6.meaning: Signs / verses / evidentiary marks — the plural of 'āyah', a sign or token that points to something beyond itself; used for miraculous signs, natural wonders, and the discrete verses of revelation.
6.grammar: A sound feminine plural. The '-in' (nunation) ending marks it as indefinite ('signs', not 'the signs') and is the genitive/accusative (oblique) case form, typical of an object or a word governed by a preposition.
6.root: ا-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token that indicates something

7.meaning: Clear, manifest, self-evident — the feminine plural of 'bayyin', describing things that are plainly evident and make matters distinct; an intensive adjective implying something that clarifies and is itself unmistakable.
7.grammar: A sound feminine plural adjective. The '-in' (nunation) ending marks it indefinite and in the genitive/accusative (oblique) case, so it agrees with an indefinite feminine plural noun it describes ('clear ___').
7.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct, evident; to make plain

9.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
9.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

10.meaning: Darknesses, layers of gloom; the manifold states of being deprived of light, whether literal or as a figure for ignorance and error.
10.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ("the darknesses"). The -i ending here is genitive — the case taken by this plural after a preposition (the -āt plural shows genitive with -i rather than the -a it would take in the accusative). The al- prefix makes it definite ("the").
10.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — darkness; also wrongdoing and injustice

11.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
11.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

12.meaning: Light — radiance and illumination that dispels darkness; often a figure for guidance, truth, and clarity.
12.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The -i ending is genitive, the case that typically follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun ("… OF …"). The al- prefix makes it definite ("the").

13.meaning: 'And indeed' / 'and truly' — the joining word 'wa' ('and') attached to the emphatic particle 'inna', which introduces a statement and strongly affirms it, adding certainty like 'surely' or 'indeed'.
13.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and') plus 'inna', a particle of emphasis that opens a nominal sentence. 'Inna' puts its following noun (the subject) into the accusative case while strongly affirming the truth of the statement.

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
14.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

15.meaning: A preposition 'bi' ('with / by / in / for') joined to the attached pronoun 'you all', yielding 'with you' or 'for you (plural)'. The exact shade — attachment, instrument, or benefit — depends on the verb it accompanies.
15.grammar: A preposition plus an attached pronoun. 'bi' is a versatile preposition (with, by, in, for), and -kum is the genitive/object pronoun 'you all' (masculine plural). Pronouns following a preposition always take this attached (genitive) form.

16.meaning: Truly most kind, compassionate, tender; one who shows raʾfa — gentle pity and clemency, an especially soft and caring form of mercy. Used as a divine attribute.
16.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿūl ('full of kindness'), with the emphatic prefix la- ('truly'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case combined with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is truly most kind').

17.meaning: Most merciful, ever-merciful; one whose mercy is constant and abundant. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's enduring, all-embracing compassion toward His creation.
17.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿīl ('abundantly/constantly merciful'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is most merciful').

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
2.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

3.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that … not,' 'lest,' 'so as not to.' It introduces a clause of something feared, intended-to-prevent, or negated after a verb.
3.grammar: A merging of the particle an ('that,' which introduces a verb in the subjunctive) with the negative lā ('not'); the 'n' of an assimilates into lā, giving allā. Together they mean 'that … not' and put the following verb into the subjunctive mood, often after verbs of fearing, wishing, or commanding.

4.meaning: You spend, expend, or give out — to lay out wealth or resources, especially in charity or for a cause; the act of disbursing what one has rather than withholding it.
4.grammar: Present-tense verb, 2nd person masculine plural ('you all'). The tu- prefix marks the present tense and the 'you' subject; the -ū ending marks a plural ('you all') subject. The form lacks the final -na of the plain indicative, signalling a 'dependent' mood — the form a verb takes after certain particles (such as those meaning 'that,' 'so that,' or in conditional 'if' clauses). It comes from form IV (causative), 'to make wealth go forth,' i.e. to spend.
4.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to spend, to expend, to disburse

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
6.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and to Allah (belongs)' — expressing ownership or rightful belonging to Allah; the lām conveys possession or entitlement.
8.grammar: The conjunction 'wa-' ('and') joined to the prepositional phrase 'lillāhi'. This phrase is the preposition 'li-' ('to/for', here showing possession) prefixed to the name 'Allah'; when 'li-' attaches, the connecting hamza and the first lām of the definite article are elided in writing, leaving a single written lām for the preposition followed by the doubled (shadda-bearing) lām of the name. 'Allah' takes the -i (genitive) ending required after a preposition.

9.meaning: Inheritance — that which is left behind and passed on; the estate or legacy that devolves to an heir after its former owner.
9.grammar: A noun, 'inheritance.' The final -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('X is …'). Built on a form that names the result of an action — here, what is left to be inherited.
9.root: و-ر-ث (w-r-th) — to inherit; to receive what is passed down

10.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
10.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

11.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
11.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

12.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
12.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

13.meaning: 'They are equal / it is the same' — to be on a par, level, or alike; to stand even with one another with no difference of value.
13.grammar: A Form VIII present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it is equal'). The 'ya-' prefix marks a present action; the weak final letter (from the root's last 'w/y') appears as the long ending. It expresses things being on the same level.

14.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
14.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
14.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

15.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
15.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

16.meaning: He spent, laid out, or expended (wealth); a verb of paying out money or resources, whether in a good cause or in waste.
16.grammar: Form IV perfect verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The a- prefix and pattern make it transitive ('to spend [something]'). The final -a is the standard perfect (past) ending, marking a completed action in the past.
16.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to spend, to expend; to be used up

17.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
17.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

18.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'before' — denoting that which precedes in time or order.
18.grammar: An adverb/noun of time. The -i ending is genitive, which here arises because it follows a preposition (commonly 'min', 'from'); it characteristically links to a following noun ('before … OF …').
18.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; the front or prior side

19.meaning: "the opening / the decisive victory / the judgment" — a verbal noun meaning an opening or unlocking; by extension a decisive deliverance or victory that breaks an impasse, and a final decisive judgment that settles a dispute.
19.grammar: A verbal noun carrying the definite article al- ("the"). The final -i is the genitive ending, the case taken after a preposition or when the noun is possessed or linked to a preceding noun ("… OF …").
19.root: ف-ت-ح (f-t-ḥ) — to open, unlock; grant victory, judge/decide

21.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
21.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

22.meaning: Greater, mightier, more immense — the comparative/superlative form of 'great/mighty', expressing that something surpasses others in magnitude, weight, or grandeur.
22.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective ('greater / greatest') built on the pattern 'aCCaCu'. The opening 'a-' is part of this 'more/most' pattern, not a separate word. The '-u' ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate ('… is greater').
22.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, mighty, immense

23.meaning: A degree, rank, level, or step — a place on a graded scale, denoting elevation or a stage above another.
23.grammar: A feminine noun ('a degree/rank'). The final '-an' (nunation) is accusative and indefinite; this ending often marks a noun specifying respect or measure ('by a degree,' 'in rank') or otherwise the object of an action.
23.root: د-ر-ج (d-r-j) — to ascend by steps; gradation, rank, degree

24.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
24.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

25.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
25.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

26.meaning: 'They spent / disbursed' — the act of laying out wealth, giving it away, or expending it, done by a group in the past.
26.grammar: A past-tense verb in a pattern meaning to spend or expend (especially wealth). The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'); the silent alif written after it is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.

27.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
27.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

28.meaning: After; afterward, subsequent in time or sequence. It points to what comes following something else. In this particular vowel-form it stands on its own as 'afterward' without naming what it comes after.
28.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u here is a fixed ending taken when the word is used absolutely ('afterward'), with the thing it follows understood rather than stated, rather than being linked to a following noun.

30.meaning: 'And all / each one' — referring comprehensively to every member of a group, 'each and every.'
30.grammar: 'And' + the totality-word kull ('all/each'). The '-an' (nunation) is the accusative indefinite ending, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). Standing alone with nunation, kull means 'each one / all of them.'

31.meaning: 'He promised, pledged, gave assurance' — to commit oneself to granting something, whether a benefit or (in other contexts) a threatened outcome.
31.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he promised.' The final '-a' is the simple past ending for a single male subject. The verb begins with the root's own wāw; the written shadda is a recitation feature (idghām), where a preceding conjunction wāw merges into this root-initial wāw — it is not a doubled root consonant.
31.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, pledge, give assurance

32.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
32.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

33.meaning: The best, the finest, the most beautiful (feminine form) — the supremely good outcome or reward; goodness in its highest degree.
33.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in the feminine superlative pattern ('the best, the finest'). Its long final 'ā' is a fixed ending that does not change for case; it denotes the utmost degree of goodness and often names the best reward or recompense.

34.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
34.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
34.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

35.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
35.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

36.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
36.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
36.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

37.meaning: Thoroughly aware, intimately acquainted — one who knows the inner reality of things, fully informed of even hidden matters. An intensive description of deep, expert knowledge.
37.grammar: A descriptive noun/adjective, 'fully aware.' The pattern (faʿīl) is intensive, conveying a deep, settled quality of knowing rather than a passing awareness. The ending -un is nominative (subject/predicate case) and indefinite — the doubled 'n' sound (tanwīn) corresponds to the lack of 'the'.
37.root: خ-ب-ر (kh-b-r) — knowledge of inner realities; being informed

1.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
1.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

2.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'this one' or 'the one' — a pointing word ('that/this') used to single out a person or thing. It often combines with the question particle to form 'who is it that…?'
2.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun ('this/that one'). It does not take case endings; the final -ā is part of the fixed word. It functions to point out or identify someone or something.

3.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

4.meaning: He lends, he gives a loan — to advance something of value with the expectation it will be repaid or returned. The verb pictures giving out wealth as a loan.
4.grammar: A present/future verb in the derived 'af'ala' pattern (causing/giving: 'to lend'). The yu- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he'), and the final -u marks the indicative mood, the plain factual form ('he lends').
4.root: ق-ر-ض (q-r-ḍ) — lending, a loan, cutting off (a portion given out)

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
5.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

6.meaning: A loan; something handed over to another to be repaid or given back later. It is the noun naming the act or object of lending.
6.grammar: The -an ending is accusative with 'tanwīn' (-n for indefiniteness, 'a loan'). The accusative is the case for the object of a verb, so this names what is being given or lent.

7.meaning: Good, fine, beautiful, excellent — pleasing and praiseworthy in quality. It describes something done well or possessing goodness and beauty.
7.grammar: An adjective ('good'). The -an ending is accusative with 'tanwīn' (-n, indefinite). As an adjective it agrees with and describes a noun; the accusative case matches a noun in that same case.

8.meaning: So that He multiplies it, doubles it, increases it many times over. The opening fa- means 'so/then', and the verb means to compound or multiply a thing into multiples of itself; the attached pronoun refers to the thing multiplied ('it').
8.grammar: Fa- is a connector ('so/then'). The verb is in the 'fā'ala' pattern (intensive: 'to multiply/double'). The yu- prefix marks 'he'; the -a ending here is subjunctive, a mood often signaling purpose or result ('so that He may multiply'). The attached -hu is an object pronoun ('it/him').

9.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
9.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

10.meaning: And for him / and he has — the connector 'and', the preposition 'for/to', and the pronoun 'him'. Together it expresses possession or belonging ('and to him belongs …', 'and he has …').
10.grammar: A small phrase, not a verb: the connector wa- ('and') + the preposition la- ('for/to') + the pronoun -hu ('him'). The preposition with a pronoun commonly conveys having or belonging ('he has', 'belonging to him').

11.meaning: Means 'a reward, a wage, a recompense'. The word denotes the due return for work or deeds — payment earned, compensation, or a reward.
11.grammar: A noun in the nominative, indefinite ('a reward'). The -un ending (a doubled-vowel tanwīn) marks both indefiniteness ('a/some') and the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or for a thing being asserted to exist ('there is a reward').

12.meaning: Noble, generous, honourable, and precious. Describes that which is held in high esteem, abundant in goodness, and free of meanness — applied to things prized and to a giving, magnanimous character.
12.grammar: An adjective on the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern (conveying an abundant, settled quality). The -un ending is the indefinite nominative ('tanwīn'): it commonly marks an indefinite word as subject or as a description asserted of something.
12.root: ك-ر-م (k-r-m) — nobility, generosity, honour; being precious and abundant in good.

1.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
1.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
1.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

3.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
3.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

4.meaning: And the believing women — the feminine plural of those who have faith, who place their trust and security in Allah and inwardly affirm the truth.
4.grammar: An active participle (one who believes) in the sound feminine plural. The prefix wa- means 'and'; al- is the definite article 'the'. The ending -āti is the sound feminine plural marker in its genitive or accusative form (the -i vowel rather than -u): it names a group of females and signals that the word is governed by a preceding preposition, oath, or verb, or is linked to a following noun.
4.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, to trust, to have faith

7.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
7.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
7.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

8.meaning: Their hands. The plural noun 'hands' carrying the masculine plural possessive 'their'; often used idiomatically for what people do, produce, or are responsible for through their own deeds.
8.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-him' meaning 'their' (a group of males, or mixed). 'aydī' is the irregular ('broken') plural of 'yad' (hand). The pronoun ending makes the whole construction definite and possessed; the 'i'-coloured stem before the suffix reflects its genitive/possessed state, the form typically following a preposition or standing as object.

11.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'the day,' very often used to mean 'today' or 'this day.' With the definite article it points to the present day as a defined, known span of time, and by extension can denote 'now' or 'the present moment.'
11.grammar: A masculine noun carrying the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' is the accusative ending; on a noun of time it commonly marks it as an adverb answering 'when?' — fixing the action to that period ('on the day', 'today').
11.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a span of time

12.meaning: Gardens — lush, enclosed places of greenery, trees, and shade; the plural of a single garden, evoking abundant, sheltered groves.
12.grammar: A feminine plural noun, indefinite. The final -un (nunation) marks it as nominative and indefinite ('gardens'), the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a predicate ('they are …').
12.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — covering, concealing (a garden's foliage covers the ground)

13.meaning: A verb 'it flows, runs, streams' — used of water and rivers moving along, and of things that run or course freely. It describes continuous, ongoing motion.
13.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person feminine singular. The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it/she' subject. The verb describes an ongoing or habitual action: 'it flows / keeps flowing.'

14.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
14.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

15.meaning: 'Beneath it / underneath it' — the noun for the underside or lower region of something, with an attached pronoun 'its' (referring to a feminine thing). It points to the space below or underneath a thing.
15.grammar: A location noun ('underneath') with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('its/her'), referring to a feminine noun. The -i ending is the genitive case, normally triggered here because words of place like 'under' commonly follow a preposition such as 'from' (min taḥti = 'from beneath').

16.meaning: 'The rivers / the streams' — the definite plural of a word for a flowing river or watercourse. It denotes large, running channels of water.
16.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the rivers'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence — the doer of the verb or the thing being described.

17.meaning: Ones who abide / remain forever — those who dwell perpetually and permanently in a state or place, without end. The word denotes lasting, undying permanence.
17.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word: 'ones abiding'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive form, used when the word is an object or governed by a preceding element. It describes people characterized by perpetual abiding.

18.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
18.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

19.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
19.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

20.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
20.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

21.meaning: 'The success' / 'the triumph' — attainment of what is sought and safety from what is feared; winning, salvation, the great achievement. With the article it is 'the (true) success'.
21.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The -u ending is the nominative case, marking it as a subject or as the thing identified (e.g. 'that IS the success').
21.root: ف-و-ز (f-w-z) — to win, triumph, attain salvation

22.meaning: 'the Most Great / the Immense' — vast, mighty, and tremendous in greatness and grandeur. As a divine name it conveys overwhelming magnificence and majesty.
22.grammar: A definite adjective/noun in an intensive pattern ('the Magnificent'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for an appositive descriptive title attached to such a subject.
22.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, mighty, immense

1.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
1.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
1.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

2.meaning: 'He says' or 'he is saying' — the act of speaking or uttering words. The imperfect tense conveys an ongoing, habitual, or present/future action.
2.grammar: Imperfect (present/future) verb, third person masculine singular. The ya- prefix marks 'he', the stem qūl carries the meaning 'say', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling a plain factual statement (as opposed to a subjunctive -a or jussive sukūn used after certain particles).

3.meaning: 'The hypocrites' — those who outwardly profess faith while inwardly concealing disbelief or treachery; the term pictures someone who has a hidden 'tunnel' or back-exit out of their professed commitment.
3.grammar: A definite plural noun (an active participle, 'the ones who dissemble'). The al- prefix means 'the'. The -ūna ending marks a masculine sound plural in the nominative case, the form typically used when the noun is the doer/subject.
3.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to tunnel through, dissemble; hypocrisy

4.meaning: 'And the hypocrites (women)' — the feminine counterpart to the male hypocrites: women who outwardly show faith while concealing disbelief. The leading 'and' joins them to what precedes; this is the definite feminine plural in the subject form.
4.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun, with wa- ('and') and al- ('the') prefixed. The -āt is the feminine plural marker, and the final -u is the nominative case, used for the subject of a sentence. (A sound feminine plural shows nominative with -u and the object/oblique case with -i.)
4.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — a tunnel with two exits; hence hypocrisy (a hidden second way out)

5.meaning: A compound meaning 'for those who' or 'belonging to those who'. It joins the preposition 'for/to' with a masculine plural relative pronoun ('those who'), introducing a clause that describes a group of people by something they do or possess.
5.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition meaning 'for', 'to', or expressing ownership/benefit ('belonging to'). The relative pronoun is 'alladhīna' ('those who'), but when 'li-' attaches to it the connecting hamza of 'al-' drops out and the two lām sounds merge into one doubled lām, so the form is written and read 'lilladhīna' rather than 'li-alladhīna'. 'alladhīna' has a fixed shape and does not change for case.

6.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
6.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

9.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
9.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: 'It was said' — speech was uttered or a statement was made. The passive form: the saying is reported without naming who spoke.

parts.en: was said (passive verb stem of the root q-w-l)
he/it (default short vowel of the 3rd masc. sg. past)

11.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice (pattern qīla) from the hollow root ق-و-ل. The passive is formed by internal vowel change: the middle radical (wāw) is replaced by a long 'ī', which marks the verb as passive (the doer is left unnamed). The lām is the third root letter, not an ending; the final -a is simply the default short vowel of the third-person masculine singular past, here used impersonally as 'it was said'.

13.meaning: 'Behind you / at your backs' — the area behind a person; figuratively, something cast aside, ignored, or put out of mind.
13.grammar: An adverb of place ('behind') with an attached possessive. The -a ending is accusative, the form a word takes when it functions adverbially (telling where/when) or as an object. The suffix -kum means 'your' addressed to more than one male.
13.root: و-ر-ي / و-ر-أ (w-r-ʾ) — to be behind, beyond

15.meaning: 'A light' — light, radiance, or illumination; that by which things become visible. Often used figuratively for guidance, clarity, and spiritual illumination.
15.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -an is accusative and indefinite, the case that typically marks the object of a verb or a complement; the final -n (tanwīn) marks indefiniteness ('a light').

17.meaning: An adverb of place meaning 'between' or 'among', here joined to the attached pronoun 'them'; together it conveys 'between them / amongst them', signalling something situated in the midst of a group or shared among parties.
17.grammar: An adverb of place (ẓarf) ending in -a, the accusative marker typical of such adverbs, indicating a location or relationship. The attached suffix '-hum' is a possessive/object pronoun meaning 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
17.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies in the midst

19.meaning: A two-part phrase 'for Him' or 'to Him belongs,' expressing possession, ownership, or that something is due to one masculine being.
19.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to/belonging to') with its vowel shifted to 'la-' before the pronoun. The attached -hu means 'Him', so the whole means 'for Him' or 'His'; the preposition signals possession or that something is owed or directed to that person.

22.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
22.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

25.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
25.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

27.meaning: "the punishment / torment" — a painful penalty or chastisement inflicted as retribution; suffering imposed as a consequence.
27.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a verb or the doer/topic of a sentence.

2.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
2.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

3.meaning: Expresses 'we are / we be' — the first-person plural of the verb 'to be / to become,' in a shortened form used after certain particles to express a contingent or negated state ('we were not,' 'so that we may be').
3.grammar: The imperfect verb 'to be' in the jussive mood (majzūm), shown by the final consonant having no vowel (the dropped/silent ending instead of -u). The jussive is the clipped form triggered by particles of negation, command, or condition. The na- prefix means 'we.'
3.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

4.meaning: With you (plural); in your company, alongside you, accompanying you.

parts.en: with / in the company of (adverb of accompaniment)

4.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment ('with / together with'), here joined to the pronoun '-kum' ('you', plural). 'maʿa' always governs a following noun or pronoun in the genitive, expressing being alongside or in company with it.

5.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

6.meaning: Yes indeed / nay, rather — an affirmative reply used specifically to contradict a preceding negative and assert the positive: 'Yes (it is so), on the contrary.'
6.grammar: A response particle. Unlike a plain 'yes', it is used to overturn a negative statement or question and affirm what was denied. It does not inflect; the final long '-ā' is part of its fixed form.

9.meaning: 'Yourselves' — your own selves, persons, or souls. The base noun 'nafs' means the self, soul, or inner person.
9.grammar: A plural noun, 'selves,' with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('your,' addressed to a group). The '-a' before the pronoun is the accusative case, marking the word as the direct object — the thing being acted upon.

14.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
14.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

15.meaning: He/it came, arrived, or came about — the act of coming into presence or of something occurring.
15.grammar: A past-tense verb with no prefix and no personal suffix, naming a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it came'). All three letters here are root letters: jā spells the first radical plus the lengthened weak middle radical, and the final hamza (ء) is the third root consonant — not an ending. The fatḥa (-a) on that hamza is simply the past-tense vocalization for a 'he' subject sitting on the last root letter; there is no separable suffix.

16.meaning: 'Command, order, affair, matter.' This noun covers both a directive that is commanded and a situation or affair that comes to pass — what is decreed or what is the case.
16.grammar: A singular noun. The final -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being described.

17.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
17.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

19.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
19.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
19.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

1.meaning: So / then — the day; a connective particle joined to the noun 'the day.' It links to what precedes (drawing a consequence or sequence, 'so / then') and names the day.
1.grammar: The prefix fa- is a connector meaning 'so / then,' marking a result or sequence. al- is 'the.' The final -a is the accusative case, which often marks a direct object or, with time-words like 'day,' an adverbial sense ('on the day').

2.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

3.meaning: To be taken, seized, or accepted — for something to be received or exacted from someone.
3.grammar: A present-tense passive verb, masculine-singular 'he/it.' The yu- prefix is the third-person masculine imperfect marker; the passive sense ('is being taken,' by an unnamed doer) comes from the internal vowelling rather than from the prefix itself. The final -u marks the plain (indicative) present, used for an ongoing or general fact.

4.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
4.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
4.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

5.meaning: A ransom or compensation — a payment or offering made to release oneself from an obligation or to make amends for it.
5.grammar: A noun naming the thing given as redemption. The ending -un (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a ransom') and in the nominative case, the form used for the subject or the thing being identified.
5.root: ف-د-ي (f-d-y) — to ransom, redeem, give compensation

6.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
6.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

7.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
7.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

8.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
8.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

9.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
9.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

11.meaning: The Fire — a definite noun for fire; frequently the term for the blazing punishment of the Hereafter (Hell).
11.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following 'n', heard as 'an-nār'). The '-u' ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action.

12.meaning: A standalone pronoun meaning 'she' or 'it' (feminine). Arabic has no neuter, so 'it' for a feminine noun is expressed with this word. Used independently for emphasis or to stand as the subject of a sentence.
12.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person feminine singular. It stands on its own (not attached to another word) and most often functions as the subject of a nominal sentence ('she/it is …'). Its form is fixed and does not take case endings.

13.meaning: Your patron, protector, and master — the one who is your closest ally, guardian, and the one who has charge over you. 'Mawlā' covers protector, helper, lord, and ally in one term.
13.grammar: A noun ('protecting patron') ending in a long -ā (the same in all cases). The attached -kum means 'your', addressing a group, so it reads 'your protector'.
13.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, allegiance, guardianship; to be a close ally/protector

14.meaning: And how evil / wretched (it is)! — wa joined to biʾsa, a fixed verb of blame used to condemn something as bad, the opposite of niʿma ('how excellent'). It expresses strong disapproval.
14.grammar: Conjunction wa- ('and') plus biʾsa, a frozen verb of blame ('how wretched is …') that does not change for tense. It introduces strong condemnation of whatever follows as its subject, the counterpart of niʿma ('how good is …').

15.meaning: Al-maṣīr — the destination, the place or state one finally comes to; the journey's end or ultimate outcome to which things return.
15.grammar: A definite noun of place/result on the pattern mafʿil, with the long ī arising from the weak root letter yāʾ (ص-ي-ر). The final -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or what something ultimately is. The word denotes the final place or state to which one comes.
15.root: ص-ي-ر (ṣ-y-r) — to become, come to, end up at

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

3.meaning: A compound meaning 'for those who' or 'belonging to those who'. It joins the preposition 'for/to' with a masculine plural relative pronoun ('those who'), introducing a clause that describes a group of people by something they do or possess.
3.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition meaning 'for', 'to', or expressing ownership/benefit ('belonging to'). The relative pronoun is 'alladhīna' ('those who'), but when 'li-' attaches to it the connecting hamza of 'al-' drops out and the two lām sounds merge into one doubled lām, so the form is written and read 'lilladhīna' rather than 'li-alladhīna'. 'alladhīna' has a fixed shape and does not change for case.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
4.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

5.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
5.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

7.meaning: 'Their hearts' — the hearts belonging to a masculine plural group. In Qur'anic usage the 'heart' is the seat of understanding, intention, feeling, and faith, not merely the physical organ.
7.grammar: A plural noun ('hearts') in the nominative, shown by the -u before the pronoun, which typically marks it as the subject of a sentence. The attached 'hum' means 'their' (a group of males or mixed group), giving 'their hearts.'
7.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, fluctuate

9.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
9.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

10.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
10.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

11.meaning: A verb meaning 'it came down / descended' — to move from a higher place or station to a lower one, also used of something sent down or revealed.
11.grammar: Past-tense verb, third person masculine singular: 'he/it descended', describing a completed action. The plain -a on the final root letter is the standard ending for this simple past-tense form with a single male/neuter subject.
11.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down, be sent down

12.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
12.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

13.meaning: 'The truth', 'the right', 'what is rightfully due' — that which is real, correct, and justly owed; the opposite of falsehood and wrongdoing.
13.grammar: A definite masculine noun (the al- prefix means 'the'). The -i ending is genitive, the case typically taken after a preposition or when the word links to a preceding noun ('… of the truth / by right').
13.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, rightness, that which is established and due

14.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
14.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

15.meaning: they become / come to be — a verb of being or becoming, expressing that a group comes into a certain state.
15.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), marked by the ya- prefix with the plural -ū ending (the closing alif is silent). The short ending (-ū rather than -ūna) shows it has been cut by a preceding particle of negation, condition, or purpose, so it reads 'that they be / they would be / they do not become' depending on that particle.
15.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

16.meaning: Like those who — a comparison particle joined to a relative pronoun, meaning 'similar to the ones who…' and pointing to a group defined by what follows.
16.grammar: A compound of the preposition ka- ('like, as'), expressing resemblance, and the masculine plural relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'). The relative pronoun is fixed in form and introduces a description; it does not change for case.

17.meaning: They were given / granted — the passive past tense of the verb 'to give/bring' (form IV of ʾ-t-y), where a plural group receives something without the giver being named.
17.grammar: Passive past tense. The internal vowelling (u-...-u) marks it as passive — the subject receives the action rather than doing it. The '-ū' ending means 'they', giving 'they were given' (the giver left unmentioned).
17.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to bring or give

18.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
18.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
18.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

19.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
19.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

20.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
20.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
20.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

22.meaning: 'Upon them / against them' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, against') carrying an attached plural pronoun referring to a group of males.
22.grammar: ʿalā ('upon') takes the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The -him ending is the attached pronoun for a masculine plural 'them'; its final vowel appears as -u (himu) to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with the definite article.

25.meaning: 'Their hearts' — the hearts belonging to a masculine plural group. In Qur'anic usage the 'heart' is the seat of understanding, intention, feeling, and faith, not merely the physical organ.
25.grammar: A plural noun ('hearts') in the nominative, shown by the -u before the pronoun, which typically marks it as the subject of a sentence. The attached 'hum' means 'their' (a group of males or mixed group), giving 'their hearts.'
25.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, fluctuate

26.meaning: 'And many; a great number; much' — a masculine singular word denoting a large quantity or multitude, joined to what precedes by 'and'.
