12.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action. The -nā ending marks 'we' as the doers. The verb often takes two objects, meaning 'to make/turn one thing into another.'
12.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, render, appoint

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

14.meaning: Hearts — the inner organ understood as the seat of feeling, intention, understanding, and faith. 'Qulūb' is the plural of 'qalb' (heart).
14.grammar: A plural noun ('hearts') with the -i ending, the genitive case — which typically links it to a preceding noun ('… of the hearts') or follows a preposition ('in the hearts').
14.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn over; the heart, that which fluctuates and turns

15.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
15.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

16.meaning: A past verb plus object meaning 'they followed him' — to follow, go after, adhere to, and conform to someone, taking them as a guide or example (the act of ittibāʿ).
16.grammar: A past-tense verb in an intensive 'self-involving' pattern (to take up following for oneself); the stem is ittabaʿ-. The -ū suffix marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they did it'), and the attached -hu is the object pronoun 'him/it'. So: 'they followed him'.
16.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

18.meaning: 'Mercy' — compassion and loving kindness shown by bestowing good and relieving hardship. From the same root as 'womb,' it carries a sense of nurturing tenderness.
18.grammar: A feminine singular noun ending in tāʾ marbūṭa (ة), an integral letter of the word. The tanwīn fatḥ on that ة (-tan) marks it as indefinite and accusative — the case of a direct object or of something granted. The wa- prefix means 'and'; the shadda written on وَّ reflects a recitation convention (idghām at the junction with the preceding word), not an assimilation of the conjunction itself.

21.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
21.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

23.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
23.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
23.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

24.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
24.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

25.meaning: Seeking, earnestly pursuing, desiring to attain — the act of going after something diligently. As a verbal noun it means 'a seeking / out of desire for.'

parts.en: seeking / earnest pursuit (the final -a is the accusative case ending, here expressing purpose/motive)

25.grammar: A verbal noun (the 'act of seeking') in the accusative case, shown by the final -a. In this role the accusative commonly expresses purpose or motive — 'out of a desire for / in seeking.' It is built on a Form VIII pattern conveying earnest, deliberate pursuit.
25.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, strive after something

27.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
27.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

28.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
28.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

30.meaning: Due right, just measure, rightful claim; that which is true and rightly owed — here used to mean 'as is truly its due'.
30.grammar: A noun meaning 'truth, right, due'. The final -a (accusative) often marks the object of a verb, and in a possessive phrase like this it commonly conveys the sense 'with the full right/due OF …', i.e. as something deserves to be done.
30.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, that which is due and real

33.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
33.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

34.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
34.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

35.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
35.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.

36.meaning: Their reward, wage, or recompense — the due return given for work or deeds. The base word denotes earned payment or compensation, and the attached pronoun makes it 'their' (a group of males or a mixed group).
36.grammar: A noun in the object form: the -a ending (accusative) typically marks the word as the receiver of an action ('the reward' as the thing given). The suffix -hum means 'their / them' for a plural group.
36.root: أ-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense for effort

37.meaning: 'And many; a great number; much' — a masculine singular word denoting a large quantity or multitude, joined to what precedes by 'and'.
37.grammar: A connecting wa- ('and') prefixed to an adjective/noun. The final -un (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.
37.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

38.meaning: 'Among them / from them / some of them' — the preposition 'min' ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them').
38.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from / of / among') with the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them'), referring to a masculine plural group. Together they often express 'part of them' or 'some among them'.

39.meaning: 'Ones who are defiantly disobedient, transgressors' — those who break out of obedience to Allah and overstep the bounds of His law. The root sense is of something departing from its proper place or rind; the term denotes deliberate rebellion against the sacred order.
39.grammar: An active participle ('one who transgresses') in the masculine plural. The -ūna ending marks masculine plural in the nominative case — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate ('they are transgressors').
39.root: ف-س-ق (f-s-q) — to forsake obedience, deviate from the right path

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: Be mindful and wary of — guard yourselves by placing a protective barrier between yourselves and harm or wrongdoing. This is the verb of taqwā: God-conscious caution that shields one from what is forbidden.
4.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group ('you all'). The -ū ending directs the order to a masculine plural 'you.' Built on a reflexive pattern (Form VIII), it conveys 'protect yourselves / be on guard.'

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
5.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

6.meaning: 'And believe! / have faith, trust' — a command to believe in, place faith and secure trust in something. Prefixed 'wa' adds 'and.'
6.grammar: 'And' (wa) plus a command (imperative) verb to a masculine plural 'you.' The verb comes from a causative (Form IV) pattern meaning 'to have faith / give one's trust'; the '-ū' ending directs the order to a group ('you all believe!').
6.root: ا-م-ن / ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — faith, security, trust, safety

9.meaning: two shares / a double portion — kifl denotes an allotted share or portion; the dual form kiflayn indicates exactly two such shares, expressing a doubled reward

parts.en: a share / an allotted portion (singular stem)
dual suffix in the genitive/accusative (-ayni), meaning 'two of'

9.grammar: The word is the dual (muthannā) of kifl ('a share, a portion'). Arabic duals are formed by adding -āni (nominative) or -ayni (genitive/accusative) to the singular. The -ayni ending here marks the dual in the oblique case (genitive or accusative), which is the expected form when the word is the object of a verb or follows a preposition. It signals exactly two units of the noun.
9.root: ك-ف-ل (k-f-l) — a share, portion, or allotment; to take responsibility for something

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: Mercy, compassion, tender care that actively benefits its object — joined to 'His': His mercy.
11.grammar: A feminine noun joined to the attached pronoun -hi ('his / its'). The -i vowel on the stem is the genitive ending, which appears because the noun is linked to a following possessor or follows a preposition ('... of ...'); the -hi suffix names that possessor: 'His mercy.' The original feminine -t- sound surfaces because a suffix follows.

12.meaning: and He will make / and He will render — Form I imperfect of jaʿala, one of the most versatile Arabic verbs meaning to make, place, appoint, cause something to become, or create a state; wa- links it to what precedes

parts.en: he makes / he will make (Form I imperfect 3rd person masculine singular, jussive)

12.grammar: This is a Form I imperfect verb (mudāriʿ) of jaʿala in the jussive mood (majzūm), indicated by the sukūn (absence of a short vowel) on the final letter lām. The jussive is used here in coordination with another jussive verb in a promissory or conditional sequence. The prefix ya- marks 3rd person masculine singular. The conjunction wa- ('and') coordinates this clause with the preceding one.
12.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, render, or cause something to be

13.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something exists or is given.
13.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). It assigns a benefit, purpose, or recipient — 'for you (all).' The suffix '-kum' is the plural 'you,' showing the recipients are a group.

14.meaning: 'A light' — light, radiance, or illumination; that by which things become visible. Often used figuratively for guidance, clarity, and spiritual illumination.
14.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -an is accusative and indefinite, the case that typically marks the object of a verb or a complement; the final -n (tanwīn) marks indefiniteness ('a light').

15.meaning: you (all) walk / you go about — Form I imperfect 2nd person masculine plural of mashā, expressing the act of walking, moving on foot, or proceeding through life

parts.en: you walk / you go (Form I imperfect 2nd person masculine plural stem)
-na suffix marking the masculine plural in the indicative (present/future) mood

15.grammar: This is a Form I imperfect (mudāriʿ) verb in the indicative mood (marfūʿ). The ta- prefix marks 2nd person (as opposed to ya- for 3rd), and the suffix -ūna is the standard masculine plural marker on an indicative imperfect verb: the -ū is the plural sign and the -na confirms the indicative mood. The -ūna ending as a whole signals 'you (masculine plural) do/will do' the action and distinguishes this form from the jussive (where -na would drop to give tamshū).
15.root: م-ش-ي (m-sh-y) — to walk, to go on foot, to move or proceed

16.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
16.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

17.meaning: A compound: 'and He will forgive' / 'and may He forgive'. It joins 'and' to an imperfect verb meaning to forgive, pardon, and cover over sins — to wipe away guilt and shield the wrongdoer from its consequences.
17.grammar: The wa- prefix is the connective 'and'. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The verb stands in the jussive mood — shown by its clipped, vowel-less ending — typically appearing after certain particles or as the result-clause of a condition ('… he will forgive / that he may forgive').
17.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, shield, and pardon; forgiveness

18.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
18.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

19.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
19.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
19.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

20.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'much-forgiving, ever-ready to forgive, one who veils and pardons faults again and again'. The form stresses abundance, so it conveys forgiveness as a constant, far-reaching quality.
20.grammar: An intensive adjective (the ghafūr 'doer-in-abundance' pattern), used as a divine attribute of Allah. The -un ending is nunation in the nominative case: it marks the word as indefinite and in the nominative, the case typically used for the subject or for a predicate that describes the subject.

21.meaning: Most merciful, ever-merciful; one whose mercy is constant and abundant. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's enduring, all-embracing compassion toward His creation.
21.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿīl ('abundantly/constantly merciful'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is most merciful').

1.meaning: so that...not / in order that...not — a compound purpose-and-negation particle: li- expresses purpose or goal ('in order that'), and the remainder is a contraction of an + lā, a subordinating particle plus negation; together they introduce a negative purpose clause

parts.en: in order that / so that (purpose preposition/particle introducing a subjunctive clause)
that...not (contraction of an + lā: subjunctive marker 'an' — with hamzah on yāʾ seat — fused with negation 'lā')

1.grammar: This is a compound particle formed from three elements fused together: li- (a purpose particle meaning 'in order that'), an (a subjunctive subordinator meaning 'that'), and lā (negation meaning 'not'). In the spelling لِّـئَلَّا, the hamzah of an sits on a yāʾ seat (ئ), and the elements are written as two distinct orthographic units (لِّـ and ئَلَّا) rather than merged into one. The verb that follows this compound particle is in the subjunctive (manṣūb) mood. The whole unit functions as a negative purpose clause: 'so that [something] does not happen.'

2.meaning: A verb meaning "he knows, he comes to know, he is aware of" — to possess knowledge or become cognizant of something.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ("he knows"), shown with the ya- prefix. The final -a is the subjunctive ending, signalling that the verb follows a particle of purpose or intent ("so that he may know") rather than stating a plain fact.

3.meaning: A people or community defined by belonging — most literally a household or family, and by extension the folk or people associated with a thing, place, or way (as in 'the people of the Scripture/Book'). It denotes those who belong to or are at home with something.
3.grammar: A singular noun (used collectively). The final -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject or 'doer' of a sentence, or a thing being named or described.

4.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
4.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

5.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that … not,' 'lest,' 'so as not to.' It introduces a clause of something feared, intended-to-prevent, or negated after a verb.
5.grammar: A merging of the particle an ('that,' which introduces a verb in the subjunctive) with the negative lā ('not'); the 'n' of an assimilates into lā, giving allā. Together they mean 'that … not' and put the following verb into the subjunctive mood, often after verbs of fearing, wishing, or commanding.

6.meaning: They are able, they have power over, or they have control — to be capable of doing or disposing of something.
6.grammar: Present/future tense verb. The 'ya-...-ūna' frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and the final '-na' marks the indicative mood — a plain statement that the action holds true.

7.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
7.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

8.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
8.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
8.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

9.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
9.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

10.meaning: 'Grace / bounty / favour' — a benefit, abundance, or excellence freely bestowed; that which is given over and above what is due.
10.grammar: A noun. The -i ending is the genitive case, which typically links the word to a following noun ('the grace OF …') or follows a preposition (e.g. 'from / by the grace').
10.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — to be abundant, excel; bounty, surplus

11.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
11.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

12.meaning: And that — a linking expression introducing a fact or clause ('and that …'); it combines 'and' with a particle that sets up and emphasises the statement that follows.
12.grammar: A connective made of wa- ('and') plus anna ('that'). Anna introduces a noun clause — a fact being asserted — and gives it emphasis, roughly 'and (it is the case) that …'. As a governing particle, anna puts the noun right after it into the accusative case.

13.meaning: A noun meaning 'bounty, grace, favor, excess given freely' — generosity beyond what is strictly owed, and superiority in goodness.
13.grammar: A singular masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -a ending is accusative, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).
13.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — excess, surplus, bounty, favor, superiority

14.meaning: In the hand of / by the power of — literally 'with the hand', often conveying possession, control, or authority over something.
14.grammar: A noun preceded by the preposition 'bi-' ('in/with/by'). The '-i' ending is the genitive case, required after a preposition; it also links the word to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship ('the hand OF …').
14.root: ي-د-ي (y-d-y) — hand; by extension, power, control

15.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
15.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

16.meaning: He gives it to him / bestows it on him — a subject grants something to a recipient; the verb takes two objects (a thing given and a person given to), and the attached pronoun here is the recipient, 'him'.
16.grammar: A present/future-tense verb meaning 'to give/bestow' (a doubly-transitive verb that takes both a thing given and a person given to). The 'yu-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The attached '-hi' is the indirect object — the recipient, 'him' (the one given TO), not the thing given.
16.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; to bring, to give

17.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
17.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

18.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
18.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
18.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

19.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
19.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
19.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

20.meaning: Owner of / possessor of / endowed with — a word that does not stand alone but means 'the one who has' whatever noun follows it, ascribing that quality or possession to someone.

parts.en: possessor of, owner of, endowed with

20.grammar: A possessive noun meaning 'owner/possessor of', always followed by another noun in the genitive. The final -ū form here is the nominative case, used when this word names the subject or is the thing being described; it inherently requires a following noun to complete its sense ('owner OF …').
20.root: — (no triliteral root; an irregular noun of possession)

21.meaning: Bounty, grace, abundant favour — generous giving beyond what is owed or merely sufficient; overflowing goodness and surplus.
21.grammar: A definite noun ('the bounty'). The al- prefix means 'the'; the final -i is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or when the noun is possessed by a preceding word (the '… OF …' relationship).
21.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — to exceed, be left over; abundance, surplus, favour

22.meaning: The Great, the Magnificent, the Tremendous — vast and mighty in rank and grandeur, surpassing in importance and majesty. It conveys overwhelming greatness, not mere large size.
22.grammar: A definite adjective (intensive pattern, denoting an inherent lofty quality) in the genitive case (the -i ending). As an adjective it matches the noun it describes in case and definiteness; the genitive marks it as following a preposition or describing a genitive noun.
22.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, mighty, magnificent; greatness
